description: Machine-readable projection of the Weft schema: node families, node types, edge types, mixins, and modeling rules. The `notes` fields are plain-language display copy for each construct; SPEC.md is the narrative source of truth.

verbTriple.gloss: intent -> act -> accountability; every clinical and operational verb in every setting is this triple with a different policy pack attached

invariant: Any agent can assert; only credentialed humans can attest.

principles.title: Two layers: knowledge and instance
principles.summary: Versioned PHI-free knowledge layer joined to a mutable instance layer only by INSTANTIATES / CODED_AS / MAPS_TO; never copy hierarchy into instances.

principles.title: Reify relationships that carry role, period, state, or signature
principles.summary: Such relationships are nodes, not edges; direct edges may exist only as derived shortcuts.

principles.title: One event shape for everything observed
principles.summary: Clinical vitals, room temps, RTLS transitions, and power states share the Event shape; raw streams stay in the TSDB, only semantic transitions materialize.

principles.title: Small closed edge vocabulary with named inverses plus one monitored escape hatch
principles.summary: RELATES_TO is the only open edge; accumulation there is the missing-schema-feature detector, reviewed quarterly.

principles.title: Space, placement, and function are three separate edge families
Temporal validity everywhere; append-only corrections
principles.summary: Validity intervals on high-churn edges; corrections are SUPERSEDES plus a new node, never deletion; unattested-work queries are anti-joins over ATTESTED_BY.

principles.title: Authority is not relationship
principles.summary: RELATED_TO is a social fact; HAS_AUTHORITY_FOR is a separate, evidenced, scoped, revocable edge via ConsentAuthority.

principles.title: Segmentation is a schema property
principles.summary: Every node and edge carries dataClass; EHR write-back policy composes over it.

mixins.name: BookableResource
mixins.notes: Multi-resource booking is atomic; Location.operationalState constrains slot generation.

mixins.name: Attestable
mixins.notes: Versions carry attestations; edit-is-attest; per-item, never per-note.

mixins.name: Embeddable
grants: versioned embeddings in an external vector index
mixins.notes: Knowledge layer only; instance nodes are never embedded (embed-don't-store). See markdown section 12.

families.name: Devices & Sensing
families.notes: DeviceModel lives in the knowledge layer

families.name: Supply
families.notes: ItemDefinition lives in the knowledge layer

nodeTypes.name: Location
nodeTypes.notes: Any place, at any scale: a campus contains buildings, buildings contain wings, wings contain rooms, rooms contain beds — each simply 'part of' the next. A place's readiness (clean / dirty / occupied / blocked) is tracked directly and controls whether it can be booked. A patient's home counts too — a place the organization doesn't control. (The place vocabulary follows FHIR R5, the only standard that goes down to bed and vehicle.)

nodeTypes.name: RtlsZone
nodeTypes.notes: A radio-coverage area from the location-tracking system, kept separate from rooms because radio zones don't line up perfectly with walls. Each zone links to the room it covers and carries how confident a 'seen here' reading is — routing a nurse call demands room-level confidence.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: HL7 RTLS IG (ballot)

nodeTypes.name: StockLocation
nodeTypes.notes: A place that holds supplies. One type covers the dispensing cabinet, the med cart, the crash cart, the vaccine fridge, the school med cabinet, the controlled drawer, a nurse's car trunk, a field-trip kit, and a patient's home shelf — what differs between them is the rules applied, not the kind of thing.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: no FHIR resource for a supply-holding place; unifies dispensing cabinet / med cart / fridge / kit — differences are policy, not type

nodeTypes.name: DeviceModel
nodeTypes.notes: The make-and-model catalog entry, identified by the manufacturer's barcode identity (UDI/GTIN). Recalls and maintenance strategies attach here — to the model — and reach every physical unit on site through it.

nodeTypes.name: DeviceRole
nodeTypes.notes: A functional slot a device fills: 'the OR 2 anesthesia machine position,' 'the ward kiosk.' The slot stays put while serial-numbered units rotate through it — which is exactly what keeps swap history intact. (The model / slot / physical-unit three-way split is deliberate and non-negotiable; manufacturing systems call the slot an equipment role, ISA-95.)
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: ISA-95 equipment role

nodeTypes.name: DeviceInstance
nodeTypes.notes: One physical, serial-numbered device. It can contain sub-components (a monitor's modules), and when it senses or acts on its own it counts as an agent — able to produce readings, never to sign for them.

nodeTypes.name: Tag
nodeTypes.notes: A tracking beacon (BLE/NFC). Deliberately kept separate from whatever it's attached to — tags get moved and reused — with each attachment stored as its own dated record (an Association).
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: HL7 RTLS IG (ballot)

nodeTypes.name: Association
nodeTypes.notes: The connection itself, kept as its own record because it changes over time: which tag is on which person, which pump is attached to which patient, which serial number fills which equipment slot. Each binding carries a start and end, so when a tag is reused or a device is swapped, the history survives. (Promoting a relationship to a record of its own is design principle P2; FHIR R5 added DeviceAssociation for exactly this.)
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR R5 DeviceAssociation

nodeTypes.name: SensorStream
nodeTypes.notes: One named measurement channel on a device: 'fridge F-2 temperature,' 'gateway G-9 signal strength.' The graph keeps the channel and what it means; the flood of raw readings lives in a separate time-series store the channel points into.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: Brick Schema Point

nodeTypes.name: Person
nodeTypes.notes: One human being, however many roles they hold — a nurse here is also a patient somewhere else. This is the single identity those roles link back to, with each link carrying how confident we are it's the same person.

nodeTypes.name: Patient
nodeTypes.notes: A person in their role as a receiver of care at a particular organization. Settings rename it — Student in a school, Resident in a nursing home — but it's the same type.

nodeTypes.name: Practitioner
nodeTypes.notes: A clinician as a person, independent of any employer. Licenses and credentials belong here, so they follow the person between jobs.

nodeTypes.name: PractitionerRole
nodeTypes.notes: A clinician's job at a particular place and time: this person, at this organization, at this location, in this specialty, for this period. Orders and actions attach to the job, not the person — so history stays correct when people change jobs. (The demo personas are these.)

nodeTypes.name: RelatedPerson
nodeTypes.notes: A family member or caregiver who acts in the record — consents, witnesses, gets trained on a skill. Someone who is merely a phone number on file stays a contact detail; they become a record of their own the moment they do something.

nodeTypes.name: Organization
nodeTypes.notes: Any organization, nested naturally: health system contains hospital contains department; district contains school. Insurers, pharmacies, agencies, and courts are organizations too.

nodeTypes.name: OrganizationAffiliation
nodeTypes.notes: A relationship between two organizations, kept as its own record so it can carry its own dates and terms: referral agreements, network membership, a hospice operating inside an SNF.

nodeTypes.name: CareTeam
nodeTypes.notes: A named team around a patient or a purpose — a code team assembled for one event, or a long-running care team. Members are jobs (or other teams), each with the period they're on it.

nodeTypes.name: Credential
nodeTypes.notes: A qualification: a license, DEA number, CPR certification, delegation training, program enrollment — with who issued it, where it's valid, and when it expires. Expiry automatically creates renewal work.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR Practitioner.qualification — element promoted to node so expiry/verification can drive workflow

nodeTypes.name: VerificationResult
nodeTypes.notes: The record that a credential was actually checked against its issuing source. Claiming a license and verifying it are kept as two separate facts.

nodeTypes.name: Encounter
nodeTypes.notes: One bounded interaction with a patient — a visit, a session, a stay — lasting minutes to days, including where the patient was throughout (bay to OR to recovery).

nodeTypes.name: EpisodeOfCare
nodeTypes.notes: A longer arc of care around one condition or program — a home-health 60-day period, a wound episode, a pregnancy — owned by one organization and containing many encounters.

nodeTypes.name: Course
nodeTypes.notes: A planned series of sessions against a protocol — 36 TMS sessions, a chemo regimen, a PT plan, a vaccine series — where planned-versus-actually-delivered is the whole point. Each session is an encounter numbered within the course.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: no FHIR container for a protocolized planned series with plan-vs-actual; generalizes ProceduralCourse (TMS/Spravato/chemo/PT)

nodeTypes.name: CareRelationship
nodeTypes.notes: An ongoing relationship with no planned end: has this primary doctor, lives at this facility, enrolled in this program, on this school's roster. Dated from-and-to; when sources disagree about it (attribution disputes), each source's version is kept side by side.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: payer attribution files + FHIR CareTeam/EpisodeOfCare fragments; no single effective-dated relationship state

nodeTypes.name: Panel
nodeTypes.notes: A defined group of people someone is responsible for: a doctor's panel, a school roster, a ward census, a caseload, a sports team, a screening cohort. One type — what differs is the basis of membership (rostered, assigned, resides, enrolled, team member). Deliberately administrative rather than clinical: this is the mental-model fact kept out of the chart.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR Group; the non-clinical membershipBasis usage is the novel part

nodeTypes.name: Schedule
nodeTypes.notes: The bookable calendar of a person, room, or machine.

nodeTypes.name: Appointment
nodeTypes.notes: A booking — which can claim several openings at once as a single unit (chair + machine + technician), so half-made bookings can't happen.

nodeTypes.name: WaitlistEntry
nodeTypes.notes: A patient waiting for a kind of appointment, with their priority and a record of each offer made.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: scheduling-system practice; no FHIR resource

nodeTypes.name: Shift
nodeTypes.notes: Who is working, in what role, on which unit, for which hours. Staffing rules (ratios, skill-mix quotas) are checked against the shift, not against individuals.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: workforce-scheduling practice; compliance (ratios, Fachkraftquote) computes over it; no FHIR resource

nodeTypes.name: Route
nodeTypes.notes: An ordered run of stops with the travel between them: a home-health day, a med-cart pass, a lab courier loop, chained transports.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: vehicle-routing / EMS CAD practice; no FHIR resource

nodeTypes.name: Order
nodeTypes.notes: An instruction that something be done — a medication, a test, a referral, supplies. Renewals and corrections chain to what they replace, so the history of intent is never overwritten.

nodeTypes.name: Event
nodeTypes.fhirAnalog: Observation | MedicationAdministration | Procedure | Specimen | ImagingStudy | SupplyDelivery
nodeTypes.notes: Something that happened, always in one shared shape: who or what did it, about whom or what, what was observed or done, when, and where. A blood pressure, a med given, a fridge temperature alarm, a room turned over, a weather advisory about a campus — clinical or not, same shape. (Design principle P3.)
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: W3C SOSA Observation — structurally isomorphic to FHIR Observation (P3)

nodeTypes.name: Condition
nodeTypes.notes: A clinical state that persists — a diagnosis, with when it began and (perhaps) ended — supported by the events that evidence it. States and happenings are deliberately kept distinct.

nodeTypes.name: Allergy
nodeTypes.notes: An allergy or intolerance — a persisting state, handled the same way as Condition.

nodeTypes.name: InstrumentResponse
nodeTypes.notes: A filled-out questionnaire or assessment (a PHQ-9, an intake form, an OASIS), linked to the exact versioned form it used. Computed scores become observations of their own.

nodeTypes.name: Task
nodeTypes.notes: A unit of work with an owner, a due time, and a status. Automated pipeline steps use the same shape to carry their inputs and outputs.

nodeTypes.name: Handoff
nodeTypes.notes: Responsibility changing hands, kept as its own record: shift report, transfer, transport, referral, discharge. It knows whether the loop closed — sent is not the same as received and acted on.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR Communication + Task; I-PASS / SBAR practice standards — promoted so loop-closure state is first-class

nodeTypes.name: CountEvent
nodeTypes.notes: A check that what's actually there matches what should be there: controlled-drug counts, surgical sponge counts, medication reconciliation, crash-cart seal checks, expiry sweeps — sometimes requiring a second person to confirm independently. One type; the applicable policy sets the rules.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: controlled-count / med-rec / seal-check practice; FHIR has no verify-actual-vs-expected verb

nodeTypes.name: TransportRequest
nodeTypes.notes: A request to move someone or something — a patient, a specimen, a device, supplies — from one place to another, with the legs of the trip and its requirements (oxygen, an escort, a chain-of-custody log).
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: EMS CAD / hospital transport dispatch practice; no FHIR resource

nodeTypes.name: Alert
nodeTypes.notes: Something needing attention — a care gap, a critical lab result, a threshold breach — that knows who it was routed to, who it was escalated to, and who acknowledged it. An alert nobody acknowledged is visibly still open, by construction.

nodeTypes.name: Communication
nodeTypes.notes: A message: a secure chat, a family update, a fax (filed with its full history), a portal thread, a parent notification.

nodeTypes.name: Document
nodeTypes.notes: A document: a note, a care plan, a consent form's paper trail — or a court order, which serves as the evidence behind a who-may-decide record.

nodeTypes.name: IncidentReport
nodeTypes.notes: An incident: an injury, a fall, a device event (the FDA-reportable kind), an unresolved count discrepancy.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: AHRQ Common Formats / FDA MedWatch

nodeTypes.name: ItemDefinition
nodeTypes.notes: The supply catalog entry: a medication, a vaccine, a wound supply, PPE, a blood product, an epi-pen.

nodeTypes.name: InventoryLot
nodeTypes.notes: A specific batch on the shelf: lot number, expiry date, quantity — and who funded it. Publicly-funded and private stock must stay segregated by law, so the funding source rides on the batch itself. A batch can belong to the organization or to a patient (a student's own med bottle).
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: GS1 UDI PI (lot/expiry); fundingSource segregation (VFC/340B/REMS) is regulatory, not FHIR

nodeTypes.name: ParLevel
nodeTypes.notes: The minimum of an item to keep on hand at a given place. Dropping below it automatically creates restocking work.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: supply-chain par-level practice; no FHIR resource

nodeTypes.name: Coverage
nodeTypes.notes: A patient's enrollment in an insurance plan — with a rank when they have several, settling which insurance pays first.

nodeTypes.name: Payer
nodeTypes.notes: An insurer. Payer networks are just organizations, and Germany's two-fund system (care fund vs health fund) is simply two payers that authorize different things.

nodeTypes.name: EligibilityCheck
nodeTypes.notes: A moment-in-time answer to 'is this coverage active, and what does it allow?' — true when checked, decaying afterward. The check date always rides along, so staleness is visible.

nodeTypes.name: Authorization
nodeTypes.notes: The payer's permission for care: what was approved, for how many units, valid until when. Renewals chain to what they replace, and the evidence packet that won the approval stays attached.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: X12 278 / Da Vinci PAS IG; promoted to a node so reauth SUPERSEDES chains and unit ceilings are first-class

nodeTypes.name: ClaimLine
nodeTypes.notes: One billed service on a claim. Each line names its billing code and rides on a clinician's signed attestation of the underlying care — no attestation, no claim line.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR Claim.item — element promoted so SUPPORTED_BY Attestation (no attestation, no claim line) can land per line

nodeTypes.name: Remittance
nodeTypes.notes: The payer's response to a claim: what was paid, adjusted, or denied. Denials chain into corrections and appeals.

nodeTypes.name: Concept
nodeTypes.notes: A standard code and its meaning (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD, or a local code). Patient records point at concepts; the relationships between codes live here in the reference layer and are never copied into patient records.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: SNOMED CT / LOINC / RxNorm / UMLS CUI — CodeSystem concepts as addressable nodes

nodeTypes.name: ProtocolDefinition
nodeTypes.notes: A reusable definition of how care should go: an order set, a treatment protocol, a standing order, a screening schedule. Applying one to a real patient is itself a recorded action — so 'which protocol version produced this?' always has an answer.

nodeTypes.name: InstrumentDefinition
nodeTypes.notes: The questionnaire or assessment form itself, versioned. Translations are validated ones only — never machine-translated.

nodeTypes.name: PromptTemplate
nodeTypes.notes: An AI prompt treated like clinical content: versioned, reviewed, and signed off. Every AI run records exactly which prompt version governed it.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR Library as container; the P&T-governed prompt-as-content practice is the novel part

nodeTypes.name: PolicyRule
nodeTypes.notes: A rule an organization sets that blocks an action until it is satisfied: witnessed dispensing, a two-nurse check, a time-out before incision. Rules stack down the org chart — which is how one schema serves every care setting.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: CQL / CDS Hooks cover fragments; org-scoped verb-gating policy packs composing down the org tree have no FHIR home

nodeTypes.name: Agent
nodeTypes.notes: Three concrete classes: human, hardware, software. See agentClasses.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: W3C PROV Agent; FHIR Provenance.agent.who

nodeTypes.name: SoftwareAgent
nodeTypes.notes: A specific AI model version — the voice extractor, the triage model, the route optimizer. It acts only on behalf of an accountable organization, and it can propose but never sign.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: HL7 AI Transparency on FHIR IG (draft)

nodeTypes.name: Activity
nodeTypes.notes: One bounded run of work — an extraction, a detector sweep, a sync job — recording what it read, which definition governed it, and which earlier run fed into it. The unit of 'how did this get here?'
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: W3C PROV Activity; FHIR Provenance activity

nodeTypes.name: Assertion
nodeTypes.notes: A claim nobody has signed yet: an AI's extracted candidate, a detector's finding, a sensor's inference. Held apart from the official record by construction until a credentialed human acts on it.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: HL7 AIAST tag (AI Transparency IG) — resource + tag promoted to quarantine class

nodeTypes.name: Attestation
nodeTypes.notes: A human signature over one specific item and version — never over a whole note at once. It comes in three modes (attest / verify / co-reason), and editing something counts as signing it. Only credentialed humans can do this.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR Provenance + Signature — promoted so mode (attest/verify/co-reason) and per-item scope are first-class

nodeTypes.name: Consent
nodeTypes.notes: Permission, precisely scoped: who granted it (not always the patient), for what, revocable, versioned — and where the law requires, controlling disclosure item by item. Missing consent blocks the action outright.

nodeTypes.name: ConsentAuthority
nodeTypes.notes: Who may decide for whom, kept as its own record: person x patient x legal basis (self, parent, guardian, POA, Betreuer, court order) x scope x restrictions, with the evidencing document attached (EVIDENCED_BY). One type unifies pediatric guardianship, custody asymmetry, POA, Betreuung, adolescent carve-outs, foster agency, LEO custody.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: legal instruments (POA, guardianship, Betreuung, court order); FHIR Consent.actor covers a fragment

nodeTypes.name: ExternalSystem
nodeTypes.notes: Any outside system we exchange with: the EHR, a school information system, a state registry, a pharmacy network, a lab, a weather feed. Nothing enters the graph without a recorded 'came from'; nothing leaves without a recorded 'sent to.'
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR Endpoint + Organization

nodeTypes.name: SyncEvent
nodeTypes.notes: One recorded act of data arriving from outside — a roster sync, a feed import.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR AuditEvent (adjacent)

nodeTypes.name: ReportSubmission
nodeTypes.notes: One recorded act of sending data out — a registry submission, a state report, a governed write-back to the EHR.
nodeTypes.standardsAnchor: FHIR AuditEvent (adjacent)

edgeTypes.name: PART_OF
edgeTypes.notes: 'Is part of' — one containment relationship serving places, organizations, devices, and encounters alike.

edgeTypes.name: IMPLEMENTS_ROLE
edgeTypes.notes: Which physical unit fills which slot, and when.

edgeTypes.name: INSTANTIATES
edgeTypes.notes: 'Follows this definition' — connects a real record to the versioned protocol, form, or prompt that shaped it.

edgeTypes.name: MAPS_TO
edgeTypes.notes: Between reference concepts (and radio zones to rooms) — never on patient records.

edgeTypes.name: IS_A
edgeTypes.notes: Between reference concepts only — never on patient records.

edgeTypes.name: LOCATED_AT
edgeTypes.notes: Where a movable thing currently is; location tracking keeps it current.

edgeTypes.name: AT
edgeTypes.notes: Where something took place; an encounter's location is tracked over time as the patient moves.

edgeTypes.name: COVERS
edgeTypes.notes: Nurse covers two schools; kiosk serves a Wohnbereich.

edgeTypes.name: ATTACHED_TO
edgeTypes.notes: What a tag is attached to; the dated binding record (Association) is the source of truth.

edgeTypes.name: FEEDS
edgeTypes.notes: Functional wiring between systems; used sparingly.

edgeTypes.name: FULFILLS
edgeTypes.notes: 'Carries out' — connects the act to the instruction it fulfills; the middle of order → event → sign-off.

edgeTypes.name: WITNESSED_BY
edgeTypes.notes: The independent second person in two-person checks.

edgeTypes.name: ASSIGNED_TO
edgeTypes.notes: Who or what a task or device is assigned to; device-to-patient assignments keep their dated binding record.

edgeTypes.name: CONSUMED
edgeTypes.notes: What a clinical act used up — the same connection that decrements inventory and supports the charge.

edgeTypes.name: ACKNOWLEDGED_BY
edgeTypes.notes: The receipt that closes the loop — someone saw it and owned it.

edgeTypes.name: GATES
edgeTypes.notes: Blocks the action outright until the rule is satisfied.

edgeTypes.name: RELATED_TO
edgeTypes.notes: A social or family relationship only — being someone's mother grants no permissions here; decision authority is a separate, evidenced record. (Design principle P7.)

edgeTypes.name: HAS_AUTHORITY_FOR
edgeTypes.notes: May make decisions for — with the legal basis, scope, and evidence attached.

edgeTypes.name: LICENSED_IN
edgeTypes.notes: Where a clinician may practice — makes 'is telehealth allowed for this patient's state?' a simple lookup.

edgeTypes.name: INFORMED_BY
edgeTypes.notes: Which earlier run fed into this one.

edgeTypes.name: DERIVED_FROM
edgeTypes.notes: What this was computed or derived from — full lineage, all the way back.

edgeTypes.name: ON_BEHALF_OF
edgeTypes.notes: Acting for whom: software acts for an accountable organization; a delegate acts for a delegator.

edgeTypes.name: ATTESTED_BY
edgeTypes.notes: The human signature — only credentialed humans, never software or devices.

edgeTypes.name: SUPERSEDES
edgeTypes.notes: Replaces an earlier version without erasing it — corrections, renewals, and resubmissions all keep their history.

edgeTypes.name: FOR
edgeTypes.notes: Overloaded across the financial and scheduling groups in v0.1; candidate for a split in v0.2.

edgeTypes.name: SUPPORTED_BY
edgeTypes.notes: The billing-integrity edge: no attestation, no claim line.

edgeTypes.name: ATTRIBUTED_TO_PANEL
edgeTypes.notes: Which group a quality measure counts against.

edgeTypes.name: SYNCED_FROM
edgeTypes.notes: Where inbound data came from — nothing enters the graph without it.

edgeTypes.name: REPORTED_TO
edgeTypes.notes: Where outbound data went — nothing leaves without it.

edgeTypes.name: RELATES_TO
edgeTypes.notes: The one free-form connection, for relationships the catalog doesn't cover yet. Uses are tallied and reviewed quarterly; recurring kinds get promoted to real, named relationships. (Design principle P4.)

settingExtensionSurfaces.mechanism: PolicyRule sets scoped to Organization, composing down the org tree

governance.fhirRoundTrip: every dataClass: clinical node/edge must map losslessly to FHIR R4 (R5-aware where noted)
governance.versioning: append-only; node/edge types carry since and deprecated markers, never removal
governance.extensionRule: product teams extend by authoring F8 artifacts (policy packs, protocols, instruments, prompts), not by adding node types

fhirAlignmentTiers.native: Maps one-to-one onto a standard FHIR record — exports losslessly.
fhirAlignmentTiers.profiled: A FHIR base type under a published profile or implementation guide (HL7's extension mechanism), or one that exists only in FHIR R5.
fhirAlignmentTiers.composite: Built from FHIR pieces — a fragment or combination promoted to a record of its own so it can carry state and signatures.
fhirAlignmentTiers.novel: No FHIR equivalent exists — the deliberate divergence list. Each entry names the non-FHIR standard or practice it is anchored to, where one exists.
